intro: The Talmud is full of stories and big ideas, but much of it is about daily life. This unit reads famous passages in paraphrase. You will see the Talmud ask what time it is, how Shabbat works, how to light Hanukkah candles, and who pays when an ox falls into a pit.

Two threads run through every passage. The first is argument: a question, a proof, an objection and an answer. The second is mercy: each ruling protects someone, such as a worker, a finder, a neighbor, or a person who might be shamed. Watch for both as you read.

By the end, you will be able to explain what a sugya is and follow its moves. You will be able to name the tractate and page of a famous passage. You will be able to say what a ruling protects and how different Jewish readers have read it.
bigQuestion: How does the Talmud turn questions about time and harm into lessons about living with other people?

timeline.t: Hillel and Shammai teach in Jerusalem
Rabbi Akiva teaches that loving your neighbor is a great principle
The Mishnah, with Berakhot, Shabbat and the three Gates, is edited
Rav and Shmuel lead academies in Babylonia
Abaye and Rava debate in Babylonia
The Babylonian Talmud reaches its final form
Rashi finishes his commentary in France
Daniel Bomberg prints the full Talmud in Venice
The Daf Yomi page-a-day cycle begins

words.d: one unit of Talmud discussion that moves by question, proof, objection and answer
the first written collection of rabbinic teaching, edited around 200 CE
the part of the Talmud that discusses and argues about the Mishnah
the passage from Deuteronomy that Jewish tradition recites evening and morning
a category of creative work that rabbinic law does not do on Shabbat; the Mishnah lists 39
a boundary that, in rabbinic law, joins spaces so that carrying is allowed on Shabbat
the four "fathers" or main kinds of damage in Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:1

test.q: What is the first question of the Talmud, on Berakhot 2a?
choices: From when may one recite the evening Shema?
Who pays when an ox gores?
How many candles are lit on Hanukkah?
What is the whole Torah on one foot?
test.why: Mishnah Berakhot 1:1 opens the Talmud by asking about the time of the evening Shema.

test.q: How many main categories of Shabbat work does the Mishnah list?
test.why: Mishnah Shabbat 7:2 lists forty less one, 39 categories of work (melakhot).

test.q: Where does rabbinic tradition find the categories of Shabbat work?
choices: in the four fathers of damage
in the work of building the tabernacle
in the laws of lost objects
test.why: The Gemara links the melakhot to the work done to build the tabernacle.

test.q: On Shabbat 21b, whose way of lighting Hanukkah candles does the law follow?
choices: the House of Hillel, adding one each night
the House of Shammai, taking one away each night
Rav, lighting all eight at once
Rashi, lighting only on the first night
test.why: The Gemara reports Beit Hillel adds a light each night, and practice follows Hillel.

test.q: What is an eruv for, in rabbinic law?
choices: to allow carrying on Shabbat within a shared boundary
test.why: An eruv joins spaces so that carrying within it is permitted on Shabbat.

test.q: Which is one of the four fathers of damage?
test.why: Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:1 lists the ox, the pit, the grazing animal and the fire.

test.q: Why does the owner of a tam ox pay only half?
choices: The ox had no record of goring, so the owner could not easily know
The ox belonged to the Temple
test.why: Tam means innocent: the owner had no warning.

test.q: How does the Talmud read "eye for an eye" in Bava Kamma 83b–84a?
choices: as a law only for kings
as payment of money for the injury
test.why: The Gemara brings several proofs that the verse means monetary compensation.

test.q: What does the case of the two who hold one cloak teach?
choices: how deep a pit must be
how to divide fairly when no one can know who is right
test.why: Bava Metzia 2a has each swear, then divides the cloak.

choices: a mark that lets an owner identify a lost object
test.why: A finder must announce an object with a siman so the owner can claim it.

choices: a person's feelings and dignity from hurtful words
test.why: Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:10 forbids wronging a person with words.

test.q: What did Hillel say was the whole Torah, on Shabbat 31a?
choices: What is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor
Each one swears and they divide
test.why: Hillel summed up the Torah this way, then told the man to go and learn.

test.q: In the porters' story on Bava Metzia 83a, what does Rav quote?
choices: Proverbs 2:20, on walking in the way of good people
test.why: Rav cites Proverbs 2:20 when telling Rabbah bar bar Hanan to pay the workers.

choices: a unit of Talmud discussion moving by question, proof, objection and answer
test.why: A sugya is one unit of argument in the Gemara.

test.q: What are the names of the three "Gates" (Bava Kamma, Bava Metzia, Bava Batra) based on?
choices: their place: first, middle and last
test.why: Bava Kamma, Bava Metzia and Bava Batra mean the first, middle and last gate.

write.prompt: What does the Talmud think a person owes to others? Choose two or three passages from this unit (for example Bava Kamma 1:1, Bava Metzia 2a, Bava Metzia 58b or 83a, Shabbat 21b). Explain what each says and how its readers have read it.
tips: Name each passage by tractate and page, or Mishnah chapter and number.
Say who is speaking: the Mishnah, the Gemara, or a named rabbi.
Show the argument: the question, the proof and the answer.
Say what or whom the ruling protects.
Describe how readers read it; do not judge the tradition.
